title: OpenSRM
description: Everything OpenSRM measures, grouped by subsystem. Panels are generated from scripts/build_dashboard.py — edit that file, not this JSON.

panels.title: Liveness
panels.description: Is the app answering, is the scheduler ticking, how big is the process.

panels.title: Scrape up
panels.description: 1 = Prometheus reached /internal/metrics. 0 means the app is down OR the metrics token no longer matches METRICS_SECRET — check the secret file before assuming a crash.

panels.title: Push tick age
panels.description: Seconds since the every-minute tick last succeeded. >300s means the Hermes cron job is dead, disabled, or the host is gone.

panels.title: Portal cooldown
panels.description: Seconds the portal budget is still locked out. Non-zero means syncs are being refused for everyone right now.

panels.title: Process RSS
panels.description: Resident memory. A number that only climbs across days is a leak; the container limit is the ceiling to watch.

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: Gunicorn runs --threads 8; a number pinned at the ceiling means requests are queuing.

panels.title: DB size
panels.description: srm.db on disk. Growth is fine, a step change means a retention path stopped pruning.

panels.title: HTTP requests
panels.description: Every request, by matched route. This is the view that answers "what is the app actually being asked to do".

panels.title: Requests per minute by status class
panels.description: Throughput split by 2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx. A 5xx bump here is the fastest signal that a deploy broke something.

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 / p99 across all routes
panels.description: Server-side request duration. The sync-bearing routes (/api/refresh, /api/login) legitimately run seconds; a jump on a static route is the interesting case.

panels.title: Top routes by request rate
panels.description: Which routes carry the traffic. Cardinality is bounded by the route table, so this cannot explode.

panels.title: Top routes by p95 latency
panels.description: The slowest routes over the window. Expect the sync paths here; anything else is a regression.

panels.title: Errors by route (5xx only)
panels.description: Only 5xx. 4xx is dominated by bad logins and bot 404s and would drown the signal.

panels.title: Unmatched requests (24h)
panels.description: Requests for paths no route handles — scanners, stale bookmarks, or a frontend calling a removed API. A sudden jump usually means a deploy removed a route that clients still call.

panels.title: Portal syncs
panels.description: The scrape pipeline: outcomes, error taxonomy, duration, and the drift signals that mean the portal changed its markup.

panels.title: Syncs per minute by pipeline and outcome
panels.description: ok vs error per pipeline (http / playwright). Playwright is archived behind a flag, so it should be flat zero.

panels.title: Error classes (1h)
panels.description: The typed error vocabulary: bad_credentials, rate_limited, portal_cooldown, busy, portal_down, markup_changed, internal, auth, captcha, other. One class dominating names the cause.

panels.title: Sync duration p50 / p95
panels.description: End-to-end sync time. The pipeline deadline is 150s; p95 approaching it means users are timing out.

panels.title: Cache hits vs joined vs real syncs (1h)
panels.description: How much work single-flight and caching is saving. cached/joined should dwarf real syncs; if they do not, every user is paying full scrape cost.

panels.title: Parse-empty by page (24h) — portal drift
panels.description: A page parsed to zero records. Alive-empty is legitimate for seasonal pages (exams outside their window); a page that is normally populated going empty is the earliest markup-drift signal.

panels.title: Scrape-lock rejections
panels.description: A second scrape for the same user while one is in flight. Sustained rejections mean users are double-tapping refresh or a client is retrying too aggressively.

panels.title: Captcha attempts per login
panels.description: Average OCR attempts to clear the login captcha. A rising average means the captcha images are getting harder or the OCR model is degrading.

panels.title: Preflight fates (1h)
panels.description: The captcha pre-warm pipeline: ready / consumed / wasted / busy / failed. A high 'wasted' share means we are pre-warming sessions nobody uses; 'failed' means the pre-warm is not landing.

panels.title: SCOPE SOAP backend
panels.description: The SRMIST-SCOPE SOAP API: per-operation call rate, outcomes and latency. Faults here never affect the portal pipeline, but they surface as empty tabs.

panels.title: Calls per minute by operation
panels.description: Which SOAP ops drive traffic. A single op jumping is usually a page retry loop.

panels.title: Outcome split (1h)
panels.description: ok / http_error / transport_error. transport_error means the SOAP host was unreachable or timed out; http_error means it answered with a fault.

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 by operation
panels.description: SOAP round-trip time. The client timeout is 15s; anything near it is about to start failing.

panels.title: Fault rate by operation
panels.description: Share of calls that were not ok. A single op at a high fault rate points at a contract change on that op.

panels.title: Push notifications
panels.description: Delivery attempts against the browser push services. Dead subscriptions accumulate here before any user complains.

panels.title: Delivery outcomes (1h)
panels.description: ok / retryable / dead / deadline / error. 'dead' is a 404/410 — the subscription is gone and gets deleted. 'deadline' means the tick ran out of time and deferred the send.

panels.title: Send latency p50 / p95
panels.description: Time inside pywebpush. The per-send timeout is 5s, so p95 near 5 means the push services are hanging.

panels.title: Delivery success rate
panels.description: ok / all attempts. A drop here with a flat request rate means the push services changed behaviour.

panels.title: Push tick throughput (1h)
panels.description: Ticks that completed ok vs errored. One per minute is expected; a gap shows up as fewer 'ok' bars.

panels.title: Database
panels.description: SQLite health: statement latency by verb, file/WAL size, and the tables whose growth means adoption — or a broken retention path.

panels.title: Query rate by verb
panels.description: Statements per minute split by leading verb. A SELECT rate that climbs without traffic is an N+1 or a polling loop.

panels.title: Query latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Statement time. Reads should sit in single-digit ms; a rising p95 on writes means lock contention.

panels.title: DB and WAL size
panels.description: The main file vs the WAL. A WAL that only grows means checkpoints are not completing — reads get slower and the disk fills.

panels.title: Row counts
panels.description: users = adoption. push_subscriptions growing without users = dead devices accumulating. push_sent_log and usage_events are retention-managed: growth there means pruning broke.
